parts.title: Fog on the Water
parts.text: Rosalind, Dev, and Callum were apprentices aboard the Silver Heron, a trading ship carrying spices across the southern sea. One dawn, a huge **galleon** with patched black sails rose out of the fog. Dev gulped. The flag belonged to Captain Harrow, a **notorious** raider whose name was whispered in every harbor. Within minutes, a **buccaneer** crew swung across on ropes and crowded the deck.

parts.title: Captured
parts.text: Captain Harrow strode aboard with a proud **swagger**, a **cutlass** gleaming at his belt. His crew hauled the spice barrels away as **loot**, and Harrow demanded a **ransom** in gold for the safe return of the ship and its sailors. He was **ruthless** in bargaining and refused to bend even a little. No one was hurt, but the Heron's crew was locked below deck.

parts.title: A Plan in the Dark
parts.text: Sneaking through the cargo hold, Callum overheard two pirates whispering about a **mutiny**. Harrow's own crew was furious that he kept most of the treasure for himself. Rosalind called it **treachery**, a betrayal of the men who had trusted him. Dev wrote a quick note and managed to **smuggle** it out inside an empty barrel that drifted toward a navy ship on the horizon. By sunset the navy had circled the galleon, and the pirates surrendered. They were **marooned** on a small, sandy island, with fresh water, to wait for the authorities.

parts.title: Back on Course
parts.text: The three friends sailed home with their cargo safe and their stories ready. Rosalind said that bravery sometimes means thinking carefully instead of fighting. Callum agreed that listening quietly had been their best weapon. Dev wrote the whole adventure in the ship's log so nobody would forget it.

definitions.meaning1: A rebellion by sailors or soldiers against their commanding officer. Example: The crew's mutiny began when the captain cut their food rations.
definitions.meaning2: Any open rebellion against those in charge. Example: The students planned a mutiny against the strict new homework rules.

definitions.meaning1: Valuable goods taken by force or stolen. Example: The pirates buried their loot on a hidden beach.
definitions.meaning2: To steal goods, especially during a disaster or a war. Example: Thieves tried to loot the shops during the blackout.

definitions.meaning1: A large sailing ship with several decks, used long ago to carry cargo and cannons. Example: The galleon sailed across the ocean with its hold full of silver.

definitions.meaning1: Money demanded in return for setting a captive free. Example: The kidnappers demanded a large ransom for the prisoner.

definitions.meaning1: To walk or act in a proud, boastful way. Example: After scoring the winning goal, he began to swagger across the field.
definitions.meaning2: A confident, show-off way of walking. Example: He entered the room with a swagger that annoyed everyone.

definitions.meaning1: A betrayal of trust; a disloyal act. Example: His treachery shocked his friends, who had trusted him with every secret.

definitions.meaning1: To move something in or out of a place secretly or against the rules. Example: Sailors tried to smuggle rare spices past the harbor guards.
definitions.meaning2: To carry something secretly. Example: She tried to smuggle a snack into the library in her backpack.

definitions.meaning1: A pirate, especially one who raided ships in the Caribbean Sea long ago. Example: The buccaneer sailed the Caribbean, raiding ships for treasure.

definitions.meaning1: Having no pity; harsh and cruel in getting what you want. Example: The ruthless ruler punished anyone who disagreed with him.
